candidates.name: Show HN: Negs (Spektrafilm) brings spectral film simulations to the browser
candidates.description: Hi HN, I'm Noah. Negs runs spektrafilm, Andrea Volpato's physically based film simulation, in your browser (it's completely rewritten in Rust and using WebGPU). Drop in a photo (JPEG, PNG, TIFF or a RAW), pick a film and a print paper, and drag the sliders. The picture updates as you drag, and nothing is uploaded: it all runs on your machine. Try it: https://getnegs.com/try/ Code (GPLv3): https://github.com/noahhaasis/negs There are also native apps on the same engine: SwiftUI on macOS, GTK4 on Linux, and Windows. candidates.name: Show HN: Brick Atlas: Browse 1000+ LEGO sets on one zoomable canvas
candidates.description: Hello HN, I’m Daniel and I run ZoomHub, a small deep zoom image service. Most online catalogs look the same: There’s a grid of thumbnails, limited to about 20–50 items, filters that refresh the page when activated, and pagination buttons to go to page 22 of 128. It has always bothered me that you can’t see the whole collection and every action makes you wait and lose context. I built Brick Atlas to show it doesn’t have to be that way: You can browse 1000+ LEGO sets by zooming in, selecting a set, seeing different angles (at full resolution) and in the sidebar, the set’s piece count, price, etc

candidates.name: Show HN: Rat Race (After Dark, 1994), ported from 68k assembly to TypeScript
candidates.description: Github: https://github.com/heyitsjames/rat-race Everything comes from the original module's resource fork. The art is the original sprites, decoded and recoloured with the module's own palettes. The music is its MIDI songs played back through After Dark's instrument samples. The rats' behavior comes from the module's 68k code, disassembled with resource_dasm and labelled by hand. Each rat is a state machine: 7-pixel steps, and every six steps a RandInt(1000) roll against its Training odds to nap, sniff or turn round. Every number cites its assembly address.
